summary: The movement to repeal women's right to vote has gained traction amongst some very conservative Christians.

summary: Wales could not emulate their famous victory against New Zealand as Australia claimed the Nations Championship spoils in Cardiff.

summary: A micro-drama will use AI-assisted technology to edit old episodes of the Australian TV soap to focus on Margot Robbie's character.

summary: Locals describe the MP, who had to have both legs amputated, as a genuinely kind person who fought for the community.

summary: The crabs were seen migrating from forests to the sea to breed on the coast of the Australian territory.

summary: Sleuths shared their "despair" when Finland's embassy in Australia's capital closed for 24 hours to hold a planning day and expressed "relief" when it reopened.

summary: Nell was walking her dog in Brisbane, Australia, when she saw a distressed koala trying to protect its joey from a python.

title: Across Africa: Tunisian photographer's family focus
summary: We bring you the stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, this summer's World Cup was about more than winning – for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive episode from June 2026].

title: Across Africa: The scars of South Africa's Soweto uprising
summary: Fifty years ago, thousands of young South Africans from Soweto protested against apartheid's stranglehold on their education and the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. What began as a peaceful protest ended in bloodshed. Also, men in northern Benin confront uncomfortable realities about the lives of the women who live with and love them. [Archive episode from June 2026].

title: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns
summary: A fire broke out on a busy highway in Egypt’s capital, Cairo, on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people after a fuel truck reportedly overturned. The suspected driver was arrested on Thursday, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.

title: 'We are not fighting culture, we fight to end FGM: It's a human rights violation of women and girls'
summary: “We fight to end FGM because it is a human rights violation of women and girls. We are not fighting culture.” Caroline Lagat, Legal Advisor at Equality Now’s Africa office in Nairobi, discusses the challenges of ending female genital mutilation (FGM) and child marriage. She points to insufficient funding, conflicting marriage laws and growing community resistance to campaigns against FGM. While acknowledging some progress, Lagat calls on the government to be "the face of the campaign to end FGM and child marriage.”

title: At least 31 killed in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns on busy highway
summary: At least 31 people were killed and 15 injured when a fuel truck overturned and burst into flames on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, engulfing nearby vehicles, Egyptian authorities said.

title: Cape Town court shuts down Ramaphosa's Farmgate scandal
summary: In tonight's edition: South Africa's president sidesteps an impeachment bid by the opposition. Also, we hear from some of the Malagasy women fighting for an overhaul of reproductive rights in their country. And in eastern DR Congo, the CRP rebel group halts its advance after coming within dozens of kilometres of the northeastern city of Bunia.

title: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners
summary: Senegal ​were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners ​on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. Senegal contested the ​Confederation ‌of African Football's decision to declare ⁠Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in ‌January's final in Rabat. Morocco announced that it would “pursue all necessary legal procedures” in response to the decision.

title: Rwanda's malaria cases on the rise: Climate change leads to more mosquitoes
summary: In Rwanda, malaria cases are on the rise due to climate change. Higher temperatures and prolonged rainfall are creating more breeding grounds for mosquitoes. According to researchers, the risk of infection could increase by as much as 20 percent by 2100 in the Rift Valley. Our correspondent Aurore Bayoud reports on Rwanda's efforts to tackle the problem.

title: Africa disappointed with COP31 outcome
summary: In tonight's edition: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has failed to reach an agreement, exposing deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. Also, DR Congo's Félix Tshisekedi and Kenya's William Ruto agree to restore relations and boost regional cooperation. And determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into a sensory room.

title: How far will Ukraine war spread? Kyiv targets Russian vessels in Libya
summary: Talk about a spillover effect. In the Libyan port of Benghazi, Ukraine is claiming responsibility for the sinkings first of a Russian warship and then a cargo vessel. That's on top of the sanctioned ship struck in the Baltic Sea that's since strayed into Finland's waters. Are these legitimate targets?

title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
summary: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, hours before a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that his country's military was behind the strikes.

title: Kenyan marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for doping
summary: In tonight's edition: Kenyan athletics superstar and reigning marathon world champion Peres Jepchirchir is banned for three years for doping. Also, South African judges leave the courtroom behind and tour a repatriation centre before handing down judgment in 33 emergency asylum applications. Plus Ghana's presidency has a new jet, but critics of the ruling party are not on board.

title: Chinese cars shake up Ivory Coast's auto industry
summary: In the space of just a few years, more than a dozen Chinese carmakers have established themselves in Ivory Coast and are becoming increasingly visible on the country's streets. How have they managed to win over a growing number of customers? FRANCE 24's Jean Barrère and Eunice Stolz-Masson report.

title: AI imagery complicates Nigeria's election preparations
summary: In tonight's edition: Concerns emerge that artificial intelligence has been used to generate fake voting profiles ahead of Nigeria's high-stakes general election in January. Also, Nigeria's mining marshal heads underground to unearth some of the people and organisations behind the vast illegal mining industries. Plus a groundbreaking archaeological discovery in northern Sudan could be the ancient site of the largest church ever built in one of medieval Nubia's most important Christian sites.

title: Francophonie summit postpones new leader vote amid DR Congo-Rwanda dispute
summary: The Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) on Monday had been set to choose its new secretary general during talks in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh. But delegates decided to postpone the election for a year after a walkout threat by the Democratic Republic of Congo amid an ongoing dispute between Kinshasa and Kigali.

title: Five EU nations unveil migrant deportation centre deal with Rwanda
summary: Five EU countries on Monday announced a deal to establish a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda – the first such facility outside the bloc. The move comes after the EU toughened its migration rules in late 2025.

title: Huge explosion at oil depot in Bangkok sends fireball into sky
summary: An explosion at an oil depot in Bangkok sent a large fireball and thick black smoke into the sky, journalists said Thursday, as local authorities urged people nearby to evacuate.

title: China to launch first space mission with a foreign astronaut
summary: Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station when the latest crew blasts off Wednesday. Ali said he would be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" with him.

title: 14 countries acknowledge ICJ ruling of genocide against Rohingya
summary: Fourteen countries from Europe, Africa and Oceania have acknowledged a landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, calling on the country to comply with its obligations under international law. The United Kingdom separately announced sanctions against five senior Myanmar military figures and said it would formally recognise the genocide.

title: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests
summary: From the unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China that saw President Xi Jinping host his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, to tough talks at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey and another week of French protests over the cost of living, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

title: Indonesia factory hit by deadly blaze: Three killed and 36 missing
summary: At least three people have been killed and dozens are missing after a fire broke out at a factory in Indonesia producing sweets and snack products. Fifteen people were rescued alive from the plant, while firefighters were still battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the blaze began. The cause of the fire remains unknown, but survivors said it started in a cooling unit on the third floor.

title: South Korean education minister resigns over AI-driven exam cheating scandal
summary: South Korea Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted days before the high-stakes Suneung university entrance exam. The Suneung concluded "without any major incidents" last week, Choi said, but he admitted to a failure to "prepare adequately in advance".

title: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations
summary: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme.

title: Shenzhen trilateral: Xi Jinping's 'masterclass in diplomatic theatre'
summary: Xi Jinping positioned himself as a great statesman when he met with the US president and Russia's Vladimir Putin for trilateral talks in Shenzhen this week. But while the Chinese president sparkled on the world stage, does he have anything to show for it? Seong-Hyon Lee, an associate at Harvard University Asia Center, tells us how the trilateral has come up short on deliverables.

title: Malaysia's unwanted refugees: The plight of the Rohingya
summary: On November 19, the International Court of Justice delivered a historic ruling: finding Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. Malaysia has long been a supporter of the persecuted Muslim minority. But its role as a safe haven is coming to an end, amid a rise in hate speech and calls for the expulsion of Rohingya via social media.

title: Was the historic Shenzhen summit a political win or humiliation for Putin?
summary: The world watched with bated breath Thursday as the presidents of China, Russia and the United States met for 90 minutes for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen. Each leader came to the negotiating table with their own motivations. But Russia's Vladimir Putin was seen as walking away worse off than his counterparts, with some media outlets reporting the Kremlin leader was "humiliated" during the talks.

title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting: Trump's recognition of China and Russia as 'peers of the US'
summary: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Olivia Cheung. The trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit was significant despite the absence of concrete agreements, according to Cheung. “The significance is seen in the precedence of the United States seeing and giving recognition that China and Russia are peers of the United States,” she explained, adding that “the image of a G3 is very significant.”

title: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast
summary: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.

title: 'Unacceptable': China, EU among major economies against new US tariffs
summary: China, the European Union and other major trading partners on Thursday criticised new US tariffs of up to 20 percent proposed by US President Donald Trump after a probe into alleged global overcapacity, raising the prospect of fresh trade tensions with allies and rivals alike.

title: Powerful US storm forces historic postponement of New York's Thanksgiving Day Parade
summary: A powerful storm forecast to bring fierce winds and heavy rain to the northeastern United States has forced the unprecedented postponement of the city's 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade, with the event rescheduled for Saturday. Officials warned that Thursday's conditions could bring down tree limbs and power lines, while posing a safety risk to the parade's giant balloons and the crowds below.

title: New US tariffs: 'Trump lashing out really indiscriminately', expert says
summary: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production.

title: New US tariffs: 'Trump lashing out really indiscriminately', expert says
summary: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. title: Huang returns as Nvidia CEO in sudden reversal after Trump intervention
summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday under pressure from US President Donald Trump, drawing approval/plaudits/cheers from Wall Street and criticism from US lawmakers. The sudden reversal was the latest twist in the fallout from Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

title: Huang’s return to Nvidia calms markets but fears of an AI bubble still run deep
summary: Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO pushed the AI computing company's stocks up more than 30 percent Monday. But the model of circular financing increasingly underwriting the AI boom still has some analysts worried that the party can't last forever.

title: US flew surveillance drone over Mexico to help capture top drug lord
summary: Mexican officials say the United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help locate and capture one of the country's most wanted drug traffickers. The operation led to the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro'.

title: Trump backs Nvidia boss's return but top Democrat vows probe
summary: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia's decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer vowed to investigate potential wrongdoing amid mounting national security concerns. Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

title: 'Maintain control': UN chief calls for creation of global AI safety framework within a year
summary: UN chief Antonio Guterres on Monday urged countries to agree on the creation of a global framework for managing the dangers posed by artificial intelligence within one year. Speaking at a summit in Barbados, he warned that taming the technology is vital if humanity is to stay in charge of its own future.

title: Israel threatens to displace one million Palestinians in Gaza unless Hamas disarms
summary: Israel's defence minister on Thursday threatened to forcibly displace one million Palestinians in Gaza if Hamas does not move to voluntarily surrender its weapons, as previously promised.

title: Iraqi court sentences 8 French nationals to life in prison for IS group membership
summary: An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life in prison and two others to 15 years on Thursday for joining the Islamic State group, as Baghdad steps up prosecutions of thousands of alleged jihadists transferred from Syria.

title: Israeli lawmakers advance October 7 inquiry opposed by Netanyahu
summary: Israel's new parliament on Wednesday took a first step to set up a state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to Hamas's unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack, a move long opposed by caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

title: Libya’s Haftar visits old foe Turkey for first time in ‘new phase’ of ties
summary: Eastern Libya military commander Khalifa Haftar met Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara on Wednesday during his first official visit to Turkey, marking a major thaw in relations between the longtime rivals. The visit came days after Ukraine struck a Russian warship in Benghazi, a port city controlled by Haftar.

title: 'We are ready to facilitate removal of Netanyahu': Head of Israel's Arab-majority Joint List
summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the head of the Arab-majority Joint List said his political alliance is prepared to play a decisive role in bringing down Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government following the recent election. "We are ready to facilitate the removal of Netanyahu" from power, Yousef Jabareen said, signalling a willingness to explore political alliances beyond traditional divisions in Israeli politics.

title: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill senior Hamas security official and six other people, medics say
summary: Israeli air strikes on the devastated Gaza Strip killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahel, director-general of the Palestinian territory's Internal Security Service on Tuesday, the ministry said. Another six people, including two police officers and a 17-year-old teenager, were killed in Israeli strikes across the enclave.

title: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"
summary: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
summary: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.

title: Iraqi security forces deploy in Hezbollah stronghold under compromise deal
summary: Iraqi security forces deployed ​in the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar, state media said on Friday, under a compromise deal brokered by Shi'ite politicians. Iraq's prime minister ordered a security intervention earlier this week after accusing the Iran-backed militia of smuggling state-owned oil worth ⁠hundreds of millions of dollars.

title: Gazans flee shelters as Israeli army launches ground operation beyond Yellow Line

The Israeli army said it crossed the Yellow Line separating Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas "to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip".

summary: Bolstered by their recent military successes, Houthi rebels this week advanced close to the southern port city of Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised Yemeni government.
